items.stem: A table must support row-level updates, deletes and querying of previous versions on a data lake. Which format fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: Delta Lake adds a transaction log giving ACID updates, deletes and time travel.

options.text: A folder of raw CSV files
options.rationale: Raw CSV has no transaction log or update support.
A single JSON file offers no ACID or versioning.
A view over plain Parquet cannot provide row-level ACID updates or time travel.

items.explanation: Correct: Delta Lake adds a transaction log giving ACID updates, deletes and time travel.

items.stem: In the medallion architecture, which layer typically holds cleaned, conformed, deduplicated data?

options.rationale: Correct: the silver layer holds cleaned and conformed data refined from bronze.
Bronze holds raw ingested data as landed.
Landing is the raw drop zone, not cleaned.
Gold holds curated business-level aggregates, built from silver.

items.explanation: Correct: the silver layer holds cleaned and conformed data refined from bronze.

items.stem: Which TWO are benefits of running OPTIMIZE with Z-ordering on a large Delta table? (Select TWO)

options.text: It compacts many small files into larger ones
options.rationale: Correct: OPTIMIZE compacts small files into larger, more efficient ones.

options.text: It co-locates related data to speed up filtered queries
options.rationale: Correct: Z-ordering co-locates related values so filters scan fewer files.

options.text: It removes the need to define any schema
options.rationale: A schema is still required; OPTIMIZE does not remove it.

options.text: It makes the table non-transactional for speed
options.rationale: Delta tables remain transactional; OPTIMIZE does not disable ACID.

items.explanation: Correct: OPTIMIZE compacts small files into larger, more efficient ones.; Correct: Z-ordering co-locates related values so filters scan fewer files.
